examples.en: On rainy days, we eat jeon.
Jeon tastes best when you eat it warm.
The jeon my mother makes is the most delicious.
At the restaurant, I also ordered a plate of jeon.
Jeon and kimchi taste good eaten together.

examples.ko: 전 부치는 냄새가 집 안에 가득해요.
examples.en: The smell of frying jeon fills the house.

explain: 밀가루나 계란 옷을 입혀 기름에 부친 음식으로, 파전, 김치전, 감자전처럼 이름 뒤에 붙어요. 짝말은 '전을 부치다'이고, 일상에서는 '부침개'라고도 해요. 비 오는 날에 전을 먹는다고 말하는 사람이 많아요.

phrases.example: 명절 아침에 온 가족이 전을 부쳐요.
phrases.en: On the morning of the holiday, the whole family pan-fries jeon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전을 기름에 지져 만들 때 쓴다.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for making jeon by pan-frying it in oil.

explain_en: It is food coated in flour or egg and pan-fried, and it attaches to names like 파전, 김치전 and 감자전. The usual verb is '전을 부치다', and in daily life people also say '부침개'. Many people say jeon is what you eat on rainy days.
